title: Final review
why: The big review of the program: telling stories in the past, talking about your plans, giving a nuanced opinion, choosing the right register and reading without vowels. The last lesson of the course, to make sure everything is in place before you carry on on your own.

{"lessons": ["

Yesterday, today, tomorrow

You've reached the end of the program: well done! This review goes back over the main tools of level B1. First, the three tenses: the past is conjugated with endings, the future with prefixes, and the present has only four forms, depending on gender and number.

TenseIwe
Pastכָּתַבְתִּי katavtiכָּתַבְנוּ katavnu
Presentכּוֹתֵב / כּוֹתֶבֶת kotev / kotevetכּוֹתְבִים / כּוֹתְבוֹת kotvim / kotvot
Futureאֶכְתֹּב ekhtovנִכְתֹּב nikhtov

To tell things in order: אֶתְמוֹל, אַחַר כָּךְ, בַּסּוֹף. For plans: מָחָר, בַּשָּׁבוּעַ הַבָּא, הוֹלֵךְ לְ־ or מִתְכַּוֵּן לְ־ + infinitive.

אֶתְמוֹל קַמְתִּי בְּשֶׁבַע, אַחַר כָּךְ הָלַכְתִּי לָעֲבוֹדָה, וּבַסּוֹף אָכַלְתִּי עִם חֲבֵרִים.Yesterday, I got up at seven, then I went to work, and in the end I ate with friends. [etmol kamti be-sheva, akhar kakh halakhti la-avoda, u-va-sof akhalti im khaverim.]
בַּשָּׁבוּעַ הַבָּא אֲנִי הוֹלֶכֶת לְבַקֵּר אֶת סַבְתָּא.Next week, I'm going to visit Grandma (a woman speaking). [ba-shavua ha-ba ani holekhet levaker et savta.]
", "

Your opinion, with nuance

To give your opinion: לְדַעְתִּי, נִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁ־, אֲנִי חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁ־ / חוֹשֶׁבֶת שֶׁ־. To add nuance: מִצַּד אֶחָד… מִצַּד שֵׁנִי… For a hypothesis: אִם or לוּ, then הָיִיתִי + present.

מִצַּד אֶחָד, תֵּל אָבִיב יְקָרָה. מִצַּד שֵׁנִי, יֵשׁ בָּהּ הַכֹּל.On the one hand, Tel Aviv is expensive. On the other hand, you can find everything there. [mi-tsad ekhad, Tel Aviv yekara. mi-tsad sheni, yesh ba ha-kol.]
לוּ הָיָה לִי זְמַן, הָיִיתִי לוֹמֵד לְנַגֵּן בְּגִיטָרָה.If I had time, I would learn to play the guitar (a man speaking). [lu haya li zman, hayiti lomed lenagen be-gitara.]

And choose the right register: סַבָּבָּה and אַחְלָה with friends; בְּסֵדֶר and אֵין בְּעָיָה with everyone; the suffixes (בֵּיתֵנוּ, לְצַעֲרִי) for polished writing.

A city is feminine in Hebrew: תֵּל אָבִיב יְקָרָה, יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יָפָה.

", "

Reading without vowels, one last time

Read this short story without vowels, then check it against the version with vowels.

בשבוע שעבר טיילנו בירושלים. ביקרנו בשוק ואכלנו חומוס. בשנה הבאה נחזור לשם.

בַּשָּׁבוּעַ שֶׁעָבַר טִיַּלְנוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם. בִּקַּרְנוּ בַּשּׁוּק וְאָכַלְנוּ חֻמּוּס. בַּשָּׁנָה הַבָּאָה נַחֲזֹר לְשָׁם.Last week, we toured Jerusalem. We visited the market and ate hummus. Next year, we'll go back there. [ba-shavua she-avar tiyalnu bi-Yerushalayim. bikarnu ba-shuk ve-akhalnu khumus. ba-shana ha-ba'a nakhzor le-sham.]

The reflexes: separate the prefixes (ב + שוק, ו + אכלנו), spot the past ending (־נו = we), the future prefix (נ־ = we) and the ktiv male (יי in טיילנו = y).

You now have everything you need to keep going: reading, listening, speaking, and daring to use everyday Hebrew. כָּל הַכָּבוֹד!
